newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call eases, SBI expected to resume lending.
newsitem.headline: Indian call eases, SBI expected to resume lending.

text.p: Indian call rates opened at 2.00- 3.25 percent on Thursday compared to the previous close of 2.00- 2.50 percent, dealer said.
The opening levels were only quotes and no deals were reported at these level, a dealer said.
"The State Bank of India (SBI)'s likely entry in the market improved sentiment, pushing the call levels to 1.50-2.00 percent in latest quotes," he said.
SBI, which could not lend in the call market since June 12 because of a strike at its Bombay office, is expected to resume its money market operations on Thursday.
The strike was called off early on Thursday.
The covered positions ahead of reporting Friday and SBI's expected entry in the market will push the rates below 1.0 pecent towards the close, a dealer said.

The securities market is expected to see improved volume on Thursday, he said. The newly auctioned 12.59 percent government stock 2004 is expected to see a selling pressure on profit booking, he added.
